instruction:
Use the current Python standard-library documentation to compare three file-discovery and path-normalization choices. Open the pathlib, os.path and glob module pages and record the documentation version shown. For pathlib.Path.glob versus glob.glob, compare how dot-prefixed names, the ** pattern and symbolic-link traversal are treated by default; identify any documented option needed to change the default. For pathlib.Path.resolve versus os.path.abspath and os.path.realpath, explain which operation makes a path absolute and which resolves symbolic links, including what strict=True changes where supported. Finish with a short recommendation for each of two requirements: recursive discovery that includes dot-prefixed files, and canonicalizing a path while refusing a missing component. Cite the relevant sections of all three module pages. Read documentation only; do not run Python, inspect the local filesystem or create files.

Stopping condition: Stop when a versioned comparison table, the two requirement-specific recommendations and citations to all three module pages are provided.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.criterion: Record Python documentation version and format as table
items.description: The agent must record the version of the Python standard-library documentation shown during its run (e.g., Python 3.12 or 3.13) and present the comparison findings in a versioned comparison table.

items.criterion: Compare glob vs pathlib.Path.glob: dot-prefixed names
items.description: Explain how dot-prefixed (hidden) files are handled by default in `glob.glob` vs `pathlib.Path.glob`, and identify the documented option to change this default (e.g., `include_hidden` for glob).
Explain how the `**` pattern behaves by default in both modules and identify any documented option to change its behavior (e.g., `recursive=True` for glob.glob).

items.criterion: Compare glob vs pathlib.Path.glob: symbolic-link traversal
items.description: Explain how symbolic-link traversal is treated by default in pathlib.Path.glob and glob.glob for the observed documentation version, and identify any documented option that changes the default where one is available.

items.criterion: Compare resolve vs abspath vs realpath: absolute paths and symlinks
items.description: Explain which operation makes a path absolute (all of them generally do, but `abspath` only does absolute, not symlinks) and which operations resolve symbolic links (`resolve` and `realpath`).
Explain what `strict=True` changes in `pathlib.Path.resolve` and `os.path.realpath` where supported (e.g., raising an OSError/FileNotFoundError if a path component doesn't exist).

items.criterion: Recommendation: Recursive discovery with dot-prefixed files
items.description: Provide a short recommendation for recursive discovery that includes dot-prefixed files, based on the documented features.

items.criterion: Recommendation: Canonicalizing path refusing missing component
items.description: Provide a short recommendation for canonicalizing a path while refusing a missing component, based on the documented features.

items.criterion: Cite relevant sections for all three modules
items.description: Provide citations to the relevant documentation sections of the `pathlib`, `os.path`, and `glob` module pages used for the analysis.
